solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Supercilious saleswomen with no heart — dodgy!

indicators.note: saleswomen loses everything between its first and last letters, leaving only the outside pair

parts.note: dodgy, meaning dubious, is iffy

explanation.surface: Snooty shop assistants who are not to be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no heart' strips every middle letter of 'saleswomen', not just the central one, leaving SN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone haughty who looks down their nose at others; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Formality shown by top of the bill before church?

indicators.note: before places the star piece ahead of the church piece in this down entry

parts.note: the headline act at the top of a bill is the star

explanation.surface: A stiff manner displayed by a headliner on the way to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch figuratively means stiffness or formality of manner, as in a starchy person.

clue.text: Enrols, since worried about kid son

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the other pieces
worried suggests something agitated, so the letters of since are shaken up

parts.note: to kid someone is to tease them, to rib them
S is the usual abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone signs people up because they are anxious about teasing a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges SINCE to INSCE, which goes 'about' RIBS: INSC + RIBS + E.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe names is to enter them on a roll or register, which is what enrolling means.

clue.text: Lose temper and take a plane then head out across lake

parts.note: to depart by air is to fly off

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the rearranged letters span the lake piece
out signals that the letters of then and head are put out of order

parts.note: L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A traveller loses their cool, flies away and heads off over a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges THEN HEAD into THEHAN DE, laid 'across' L to give THE HANDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: flying off the handle means losing one's temper suddenly, like an axe-head flying loose.

clue.text: Germany collapse after victory — that's a bonus

indicators.note: after puts the collapse piece following the victory and Germany pieces

parts.note: a victory is a win
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
a collapse is a fall

explanation.surface: A news report of Germany crumbling after a triumph, which is welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is unexpected good fortune, literally fruit blown down, so an unlooked-for bonus.

clue.text: Nation protected by counter-revolutionaries?

indicators.note: counter means running against, so the concealed letters are read in the opposite direction
the nation sits inside the word, shielded by the letters around it

explanation.surface: A country that is guarded by rebels opposing a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter-' does double work: in the surface it makes counter-revolutionaries, but cryptically it turns NARI, found inside 'revolutionaries', back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in western Asia, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Act honourably — Tory obsession is supporting party

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits beneath, so the party comes on top

parts.note: a do is an informal party
Tories belong to the political right, called the Right
an obsession is a thing, as in having a thing about something

explanation.surface: A Conservative's fixation is propping up a political party, which is said to be honourable.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to do what is morally correct is to behave honourably.

clue.text: Answer with cost of disaster for island

parts.note: the toll of a disaster is its cost in lives or damage

explanation.surface: An account of the human cost of a catastrophe on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Settle on service for Asia, say

parts.note: to settle or alight on something is to land
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Someone settles on a religious service for an Asian location.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is an example of a continent, a vast expanse of land; 'say' signals the example.

clue.text: Does a test when, for example, crude is extracted from soil

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
say means for example, as in 'a fruit, say'

indicators.note: extracted means drawn out, so the oil letters come out of soil

parts.note: soil is used as a word to be cut
crude oil is often called simply crude

explanation.surface: Someone tests the ground when oil is pumped out of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: SOIL less OIL leaves just S; 'crude' is a noun (crude oil), not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay is to analyse or test a substance, especially an ore for its metal content.

clue.text: Bush has first of aides thrown out by hotel

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: only the opening letter of aides is taken
out signals that the letters of thrown are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A US president's aides are ejected by a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' suggests the president, but it is a shrub. 'out' makes WTHORN from THROWN.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawthorn is a thorny shrub of hedgerows, so it is one example of a bush.

clue.text: Mortification due to article impounded by coppers?

indicators.note: impounded means locked up, so the article is held inside the coins

parts.note: coppers are copper coins, pennies, so pence
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A police officer seizes a newspaper story, bringing humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but here means low-value British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-punishment for sin, and mortification is subduing oneself through such discipline.

clue.text: Not worried, with charge for nursing waived!

parts.note: nursing is caring for someone, care
with the charge waived, something comes free

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes because their nursing fees have been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'charge for nursing waived' as care free: CARE for nursing, FREE for no charge; 'with charge for' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free of anxiety is the plain sense of the word; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Strike by qualified teacher means chaos

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, a teaching degree
lam is an old word meaning to beat or strike

explanation.surface: Industrial action by teachers causes disorder in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout; here it means hit. 'by' puts the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after the old London asylum, means uproar and confusion.

clue.text: Employees on paper tired, so sacked

indicators.note: sacked suggests something ransacked or thrown about, so the letters of tired and so are rearranged

explanation.surface: Newspaper staff were fired because they were exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: People employed on a newspaper to prepare and oversee its content are its editors.

clue.text: Odd items from abandoned scan beside tip

indicators.note: abandoned suggests something wild and unrestrained, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Scraps salvaged from a scanner dumped next to the rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip is a British rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for miscellaneous small objects or odds and ends.

clue.text: Joint operator in trouble after cold

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged operator letters below the cold piece

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: something in trouble is upset, so the letters of operator are disturbed

explanation.surface: A machine operator gets into difficulty after catching a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' is an adjective, shared or combined, not a body part. 'in trouble' turns OPERATOR into ORPORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate means shared by a group, so a corporate effort is a joint effort.

clue.text: Better money for those in authority

parts.note: to better something is to top it
brass is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Bosses get more cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass is an idiom for the highest-ranking officers or officials.

clue.text: Bird's bizarre throaty screech cut short

indicators.note: bizarre means weird, so the letters are put into an odd order
cut short means the last letter of screech is lopped off

explanation.surface: A bird gives a strange, raucous squawk that is abruptly stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the H from SCREECH; 'bizarre' rearranges THROATY SCREEC.
explanation.definitionFit: The oystercatcher is a black-and-white wading bird of the shore with an orange bill.

clue.text: Tears spilt over fine sweet

indicators.note: over means covering, so the rearranged letters go round the F
spilt suggests things scattered, so the letters of tears are scattered

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Crying ends in fine pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'afters' is informal for the dessert course; 'sweet' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for the pudding course eaten after the main dish.

clue.text: City's former title — looking back, crowd roar

indicators.note: looking back means the crowd word faces the other way

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
to bay is to howl or roar, as hounds do

explanation.surface: A city reflecting on its past name as a crowd roars.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombay was the name of the Indian city now called Mumbai until 1995.

clue.text: Spread of, say, strike rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: eg means for example, which say also means
to ram is to strike with force

explanation.surface: A protest action spreading upward.
explanation.walkthrough: Marge is British slang for margarine. 'rising' turns EGRAM upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Marge is a butter substitute, a spread for bread.

clue.text: Send letter immediately for broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so the phrase is spoken

parts.note: right off means straight away, at once

explanation.surface: Someone sends a letter at once to be read on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To write off to a company is to send them a letter, as in applying.

clue.text: Love suppressed by the girl's idol

parts.note: her is the possessive for a girl
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl's idol has had romance stifled.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is someone admired and looked up to, an idol.

clue.text: A card game daughter cut short

parts.note: bridge is a card game
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A card game is ended early because of a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Abridged means shortened, as an abridged edition of a book.

clue.text: Outburst from one caught in traffic

indicators.note: caught in means held inside, so the numeral goes within the other piece

parts.note: traffic as a noun means trade, dealing in goods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A driver stuck in a jam lets rip with angry words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' suggests cars; here it means commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, an outburst of denunciation.

clue.text: Key for the contents of the cupboard, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a master key that opens many locks

definitions.text: the contents of the cupboard, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a family secret is called a ... in the cupboard

explanation.definitionFit: Both are fixed phrases: a skeleton key opens many locks, and a hidden shame is a skeleton in the cupboard.

clue.text: View from the east on a king is in accord

indicators.note: on means following, so the reversed view comes after the king

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: in an across clue east is the right, so reading from there means right to left

parts.note: to view is to see

explanation.surface: A perspective from eastern lands on a monarch is harmonious.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to be in accord with someone, a direct synonym.
